file: Data Analysis and Management using Hadoop & Hive.docx
items: Create a directory in HDFS
scripts/run_hadoop.sh creates a run-specific HDFS raw directory and uploads bank.csv with hdfs dfs -put. Capture mkdir/put/ls and record the RAW_PATH printed at the end. Validate the CSV first.
Write a MapReduce program in Python
MR01: mapper.py --task balance_by_job; reducer output is key, sum, nonmissing count, mean. Explain why sum/count combiners preserve weighted means. Capture code and all reducer partitions.
Write another MapReduce program
MR02: --task housing_by_education groups by education|housing. Count is column 3; unknown housing is a separate bucket. Capture counters and output.
Perform a MapReduce job
MR03: --task contacts_by_month groups by month|y. Sum/count are contact-record counts, not unique-person counts; no client ID is available.
Analyze the average duration
MR04: --task duration_by_poutcome calculates mean contact seconds for each previous campaign outcome. This is not transaction duration.
Examine the relationship
MR05: --task balance_by_age summarizes average balance for <30, 30-60, >60 age groups. Complement with H09/EDA09 Pearson correlation. Report observed values without claiming causality.
Create a Hive database
H01: hive/01_tables.hql creates banking_data. Run using beeline and the RAW_PATH printed by run_hadoop.sh. Capture database/table creation.
Define and create a Hive table
H01: client_info_raw uses OpenCSVSerde strings to parse quoted CSV; client_info stores typed INT/BIGINT/STRING columns as ORC. Capture DESCRIBE banking_data.client_info.
Load the data
H01: external raw table points at the uploaded HDFS directory; INSERT OVERWRITE TABLE client_info casts into ORC. This refreshes the project's derived table; compare raw/typed row counts.
Write a HiveQL query to count
H02 in hive/02_analysis.hql: total row count. Include query and actual count.
Display the first 10
H02: SELECT * LIMIT 10; order is unspecified because no unique row ID exists.
Retrieve all records
H03: marital='married' AND loan='yes'. Capture query/output; retain complete results remotely if longer than the screenshot.
List the top 10
H04: descending balance with job/marital fields. These are records, not necessarily 10 distinct clients.
Calculate the average age
H05: average age and record count by job.
Find the total number
H06: existing credit default='yes', grouped by education. This is not a future-default prediction.
Identify the top 5
H07: rank average balance and report subscription percentage for those job categories, with category counts.
Determine the month
H08: contact count descending and current subscription success percentage; ties break alphabetically.
Calculate the correlation
H09: CORR(age,balance), Pearson correlation. Undefined for constant variables; association is not causation.
Analyze the year-over-year
H10 is explicitly not identifiable: bank.csv lacks year or contact_date. Do not invent years or infer them from row order. Obtain an observed dated dataset before completing a real YoY analysis.
Identify any unusual patterns

H11: education balance summaries and descriptive z-scores of group means. Bank balance is described as average yearly balance, but no longitudinal annual series exists. Flag candidates for review, not proven anomalies.
Analyze the impact
H12: current subscription percentage for each poutcome, including unknown. Discuss observed association and counts.
Compare the average contact duration
H13: mean contact seconds for y=yes versus y=no. Duration is post-call information and is excluded from pre-call prediction by default.
Load the bank.csv
src/eda.py via spark_job.py eda; 01_preview.csv and printed schema. Use real bank.csv, not bank-additional.csv.
Perform basic data inspection
01_preview.csv, 01_numeric_summary.csv, and 01_quality.json show rows, numeric summaries, and missing values. Capture printed schema.
Filter the dataset
02_balance_over_threshold.csv contains a bounded preview of balance>1000. Change --balance-threshold if needed; source DataFrame filtering processes all rows.
Extract the month
02_04_06_engineered_columns.csv maps month abbreviations to month_number and ceil(month_number/3) as quarter. There is no full contact date/year.
Group the data by job
03_job_balance_age.csv contains average balance and approximate median age (percentile_approx accuracy 10000). Explain the approximation.
Find the total number
03_subscribers_by_marital.csv counts y=yes by marital status.
Write a UDF
banklib.age_group is registered as a Spark Python UDF: age<30, 30<=age<=60, age>60; null age becomes unknown. Engineered output demonstrates its use.
Calculate the subscription rate
05_education_subscription.csv contains record counts and subscription percentages by education.
Identify the top 3

05_top3_credit_default_jobs.csv ranks observed existing-credit-default rates. Unknown default statuses are excluded from the rate denominator. Loan-specific defaults cannot be established from this field.
Concatenate the
02_04_06_engineered_columns.csv includes job_marital using concat_ws.
Use string functions
02_04_06_engineered_columns.csv includes contact_upper using upper().
Convert the Spark DataFrame
export() calls toPandas only on bounded samples and small aggregates, rather than collecting an unbounded dataset. This fulfills conversion while limiting driver memory.
Create a bar plot
07_job_counts.png and corresponding CSV show clients by job.
Analyze which month
08_month_contacts.csv and 08_busiest_month.csv include contacts and success percentage.
Find the average duration
08_duration_by_subscription.csv reports mean contact seconds, grouped by y.
Calculate the correlation coefficient
09_age_balance_correlation.json reports Pearson r on complete age/balance pairs. Discuss direction and strength from the actual output.
Analyze the proportion
10_credit_default_counts.csv contains default counts and proportions; 10_credit_default_counts.png plots counts. Keep unknown as a separate category.
Investigate which contact method
11_contact_success.csv ranks subscription success percent by contact, with sample sizes. Observational differences are not causal effects.
Calculate the average account balance
12_sql_age_balance.csv comes from a Spark temporary view and SQL GROUP BY age_group. Include the SQL and observed table.
Load the bank.csv
spark_job.py train uses the shared CSV schema and validation.
Perform basic exploratory
Printed schema, 01_preview.csv, and the separate EDA outputs provide initial exploration.
Handle missing values
Numeric medians fit inside every CV training fold; blank/?/NA/null numerical values are treated as missing. Categorical missing becomes unknown; unseen categories are retained.
Handle Outliers

02_preprocessing.json reports training-only IQR outlier counts. Fixed signed log(balance) and log1p count transforms reduce extreme influence while retaining legitimate high/negative balances. No test-set quantiles are learned.
Convert categorical
StringIndexer(handleInvalid=keep) and OneHotEncoder encode all nine categorical predictors; the target is deterministically yes=1/no=0.
Create a feature vector

VectorAssembler combines imputed transformed numerical columns, contacted_before, and encoded categoricals. Duration is excluded for pre-call prediction; --include-duration is a separately labeled retrospective variant.
Choose a classification
Logistic regression is a scalable distributed baseline with interpretable conditional coefficients and regularization. It estimates subscription, not credit risk or market prices.
Split the data

A deterministic seeded row hash gives approximately 80/20 train/test after exact duplicate removal; duplicate rows cannot cross boundaries. It is not a temporal split because reliable dates are unavailable.
Train the model
The full pipeline is fit within each CV fold, then the selected pipeline refits on the whole training split. pipeline/ stores the fitted Spark PipelineModel for streaming.
Evaluate the model

06_metrics.json reports ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, accuracy, positive-class precision/recall/F1, confusion counts, prevalence, and always-no baseline. Interpret PR-AUC and recall in light of imbalance; the fixed threshold is 0.5.
Perform hyperparameter

ParamGridBuilder explores regParam=[0.01,0.1] and elasticNetParam=[0,0.5]; CrossValidator defaults to three folds, parallelism=1 and collectSubModels=False. Select using mean PR-AUC; test data remains untouched during selection.
Analyze the feature

08_coefficients.json maps logistic coefficients to assembled feature names and includes the intercept. Magnitudes are affected by units and transformed scales; associations do not imply causal effects.
Implement a Spark Streaming application

scripts/replay.py atomically publishes bounded chunks of bank.csv as JSON with unique event_id and simulated UTC event_time. Run spark_job.py stream with the saved pipeline. This replays marketing/contact records, not actual payments.
Use Spark Streaming
job_means console query reports cumulative event counts, average account balance, and average contact duration by job. State is bounded by job categories; duration is not actual transaction duration.
Develop a machine learning model
Historical training is provided by spark_job.py train. Use the resulting pipeline directory; pre-call features exclude duration by default.
Integrate the trained model

PipelineModel.load transforms every valid incoming event. predictions/ contains append-only Parquet with event_id, timestamp, source fields, prediction, and probability. Labels are optional and are never a feature.
Implement window operations
window_10s and window_60s console queries use tumbling event-time windows, event counts, and mean balances, with a 20-second watermark and update output mode.
Write a brief analysis

Capture several successive windows and query_progress.jsonl. Report observed count/balance changes, compare 10s versus 60s smoothing, and note that timestamps/arrival ordering are synthetic. No factual trends are prefilled.
Modify your Spark Streaming

Replay emits 8-second out-of-order and 90-second-late events after the first two chunks. withWatermark(event_time,20 seconds) bounds window state. The watermark follows observed event-time progress, not wall time; >20s-late records may be dropped by windows but remain in raw predictions/all-time job aggregates. Inspect eventTime.watermark and stateOperators.numRowsDroppedByWatermark in progress logs; actual drops depend on microbatch ordering.

file: Efficient Data Handling through Data Parallelism.docx
items: Load the
01_preview.csv and printed rows demonstrate validated Spark DataFrame loading.
Implement a method

Round-robin repartition(n) balances row counts without concentrating common job categories on one partition. 01_partition_sizes_N.csv records actual partition sizes. Aggregation later shuffles by job; adaptive execution can coalesce shuffle partitions.
Identify and calculate
02_parallel_job_balance.csv uses distributed groupBy(job).avg(balance); benchmark repeats partition grids without replicating the dataset. Compare actual medians and invariant aggregate outputs.
Perform a parallel operation

Loan amount is absent: loan is yes/no. 02_top5_loan_holder_age_bands.csv ranks decade age bands by personal-loan-holder counts and shows average account balance separately. This is a labeled proxy, not a solution for unavailable loan amounts.
Choose a classification
Logistic regression uses distributed optimization and offers interpretable coefficients. It handles the binary subscription target; the main modeling module supplies cross-validation.
Partition the dataset

03_04_partitioned_model.json records the partitioned training model and held-out metrics. Approximately 80/20 deterministic split; training repartitions to the largest grid size. Explain shuffle overhead, skew, sparse feature size, and driver/executor memory limits.
Implement resource monitoring

resource_samples.json samples driver Python CPU/RSS, local JVM child RSS, host CPU/memory each second. Spark UI/event logs supply executor CPU time, GC, memory/spill, shuffle, and task metrics. Local driver metrics do not measure remote executors; fill observations from actual runs.
Manage multiple parallel tasks

06_scheduled_tasks.json comes from two bounded independent preprocessing actions launched with InheritableThread and separate FAIR scheduler pools/job groups. CV parallelism is independently limited to avoid oversubscription. Show Spark UI jobs/stages and discuss measured resource contention.
